tiles: Reading into Mucha and early Art Nouveau
The organic line as a philosophy, not a decoration
A small set of images I'd happily put on a wall
challenge: Art Nouveau has always fascinated me — the flowing line, the botanical detail, the sense that design could feel optimistic and hand-made even in a mechanical age. I wanted to actually learn what made it work, not just borrow its surface.
approach: I researched the movement (Mucha especially, but also the broader turn toward nature and ornament around 1900), then drafted many variations trying to catch that specific balance — elegant without being precious, decorative without being busy. I kept the pieces that felt like they captured the spirit of the era and that I personally found beautiful.
result: What's here is a small, curated set — the ones where I felt I'd learned something about how Art Nouveau thinks, and that I enjoy looking at. They're available as prints if anyone else responds to them the way I did.
